To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most accurate metric for the evaluation of 3-D processing algorithms is the one based on the visual perception of 3-D shape, and that the best metric for this purpose is the one based the visual perception of depth.

the most accurate metric for the evaluation of 3-D geometry processing algorithms is the one based on the perceptual evaluation of the visual impairment, and the one that best fits the needs of the computer graphics community is the perceptual metric that uses a 3-D rendering engine as a front-end to the metric.

the following issues: (1) What are the most relevant perceptual and cognitive processes that affect the perception of 3-D geometry? (2) What are the existing perceptually-based 3-D metrics? (3) What are their differences and similarities?

the following questions: What is the behavior of perceptual measures for 3-D objects? Which are the most appropriate perceptual measures for a given scenario? What are the differences among the existing perceptual measures?
the following questions: 1) How do perceptually-based metrics behave in different visual scenarios? 2) How do perceptual and geometric metrics compare with each other?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most accurate metric for 3-D mesh processing evaluation depends on the specific scenario under consideration.
the best metric depends on the application and the scenario.

the most appropriate measure depends on the specific application and on the specific visual impairment that is considered, and that the best choice should be taken from the wide set of existing measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perceptually-based metrics that are more sensitive to visual impairment of 2.5-D objects are also more sensitive to visual impairments of 3-D meshes.

, in general, the most accurate metric for each scenario is the one that is based on the perceptual and cognitive mechanism that is used by the human visual system to perceive the corresponding 3-D property.
the best metric depends on the scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most accurate metric is not always the most suitable, as it is highly dependent on the specific scenario under analysis.
, although all the considered metrics provide good results for the considered scenarios, no one of them is able to provide good results in all of them.
, in order to properly evaluate a mesh processing algorithm, one should consider the visual impairment scenario that is more suitable for the specific application.
